audits.resolution_reason: Non-X distractor separates authority from a component-center rival but is outside the declared validator domain. Intended-domain decision needed; not a reproduced accepted-grid label defect.
audits.text:
## 7a41ac31fabf

**Suspected shortcut / domain restriction, not an accepted-grid label defect.**
The current generator and validator admit only exact nonzero X motifs and reject
any nonzero distractor. Consequently, the rival “for every nonzero 8-connected
component, replace its bounding-box center with 8” agrees on the generated domain,
even though the intended rule targets X motifs rather than arbitrary components.

A 5×7 reference-lawful counterexample contains one color-2 X and an isolated
color-5 cell at `(0,6)`. The selected Racket rule (hash `c86365e6748d`) changes
only the X center `(2,2)` to 8 and leaves the isolated 5 unchanged; the rival also
changes `(0,6)` to 8. The validator rejects this witness with
`found nonzero cells outside the detected X motif footprints`, so the evidence is
a teaching/distribution limitation outside the documented generator domain, not
a mislabeled accepted sample.

Exact input, Racket output, rival output, difference cell, hashes, and command are
retained in:

- `checks/audit/7a41ac31fabf/finding.json`
- `checks/audit/7a41ac31fabf/input.json`
- `checks/audit/7a41ac31fabf/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/7a41ac31fabf/rival.json`

Suggested future review: decide whether distractors belong to the intended task
manifold. If yes, add lawful non-X components and a validator/rival witness; if
no, document that the generated task teaches “all objects are X motifs” and avoid
claiming separation from component-center shortcuts.
